notice: This archive records exploratory ideas that sit outside AURORA's primary research program. None of these mechanisms has been demonstrated within AURORA, and none of them is part of the results reported elsewhere on this site.

entries.title: Holographic phase recovery
entries.established: Digital holography and iterative phase-retrieval algorithms (such as Gerchberg–Saxton) can recover optical phase from intensity measurements under suitable constraints.
entries.hypothesis: Phase information, normally discarded by intensity-only sensors, might add observables that reduce retrieval ambiguity.
openQuestions: Is phase recoverable under natural, partially coherent illumination?
Would it add independent information relative to spectral and polarimetric channels?

entries.title: Magnetic reconfiguration
entries.established: Magneto-optic effects such as Faraday rotation are well characterized, and magnetic actuation is widely used for small mechanisms.
entries.hypothesis: Magnetically switched optical elements could allow fast reconfiguration of a measurement setup without large moving parts.
openQuestions: Thermal and stray-field effects on other measurements

entries.title: Crystal-based optical materials
entries.established: Birefringent and nonlinear crystals have well-known wavelength- and polarization-dependent optical properties.
entries.hypothesis: A set of crystal elements might serve as selectable spectral or polarization filters for adaptive band selection.
openQuestions: Spectral selectivity versus thin-film interference filters

entries.title: Water-based optics
entries.established: Liquid and electrowetting lenses with tunable focal length exist; the refractive index of water is well characterized.
entries.hypothesis: Liquid optical elements might provide low-cost tunable optics for adaptive measurement configurations.
openQuestions: Stability under vibration and temperature change
Absorption of water in the near-infrared

entries.title: Optical angular momentum
entries.established: Light can carry spin angular momentum (polarization) and orbital angular momentum associated with helical wavefronts.
entries.hypothesis: Orbital-angular-momentum observables might carry information about scattering media not captured by intensity or polarization.
openQuestions: Whether natural scattered light retains measurable OAM structure

entries.title: Noble gas optical properties
entries.established: Noble gases have precisely known refractive indices and discrete emission lines, which are routinely used for wavelength calibration.
entries.hypothesis: Noble-gas references might support onboard calibration and drift detection.
openQuestions: Practicality of an onboard reference cell
Whether this improves on existing calibration methods

entries.title: Bio-inspired optical architectures
entries.established: Some animals, such as mantis shrimp and many insects, have polarization-sensitive or many-channel visual systems with documented anatomy.
entries.hypothesis: Biological sensing strategies might suggest efficient channel designs or attention-like adaptive sampling.
openQuestions: Which biological principles transfer to engineered instruments
Risk of analogy without measurable benefit

entries.title: Alternative resonant geometries
entries.established: Optical (for example, Fabry–Pérot) and acoustic (for example, Helmholtz) resonators have well-understood frequency selectivity set by geometry.
entries.hypothesis: Alternative resonator geometries might provide compact, selectable optical or acoustic channels.
openQuestions: Benefit versus conventional filters and transducers
